content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: current staffing is predicted to hold 87.0% service level from 14:30 to 20:00, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"The absences are mostly bus-strike lateness: 14 of 19 on payments and 7 of 10 on general. Payments volume is also 12% below forecast. Without any changes, service level is predicted at 87.0% overall, with payments at 82.7% and general at 92.8%. Abandon rate is predicted at 3.4%. Both queues clear the 80% target, so this is the cheapest plan that meets policy. Escalation is not needed.","trade_offs":["The no-cost plan P1 (break delays, cross-skill moves, callbacks) actually predicts lower service, 85.4% overall and payments at 80.1%. It adds disruption for no gain.","Low-cost plan P3 (₹768) lifts the window to 87.9% (payments 83.3%) and cuts abandons to 3.2%. That is a marginal gain for the spend.","Overtime plan P2 (₹2,520) gives 89.5% (payments 85.5%) and 2.7% abandons. It buys extra margin for payments customers.","The full combined plan P4 (₹3,288) is strongest at 92.4% (payments 90.4%) with 1.7% abandons. It also costs the most and moves 3 agents off general."],"watch":"Payments has the thinnest margin at 82.7%. Check that late agents are actually arriving as the strike clears. Also watch general's handle time, which has run 15% above forecast for the last two intervals. If either persists, consider P3 or P2 as the next step up."}
